discussion: The public check on candidate 8b8079f1 establishes the test contribution, and I'll conclude without an operation. What it proves: (1) The regression passes on the repair — candidate_tests reports 356 tests (the 355 upstream plus the one added), 0 failures, 0 errors, while upstream itself passes 355/355 and the 8-test contract passes, so the library, existing behavior, and unrelated tests are intact. (2) The test exposes the original problem through the original parsing path, not via a missing symbol: new_tests_on_original shows the single error's traceback entering the original parser from the test's read_string call (test line 1855) via read_string (original line 710) -> read_file (705) -> _read (1039), where it dies with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'append' — the original code appending to cursect[optname] after it was set to None for the valueless option. Because that AttributeError propagates out of read_string itself (assertRaises re-raises a non-ParsingError), the failure happens before the test ever evaluates its reference to configparser.MultilineContinuationError, so the exposure is not an artifact of the new exception symbol being absent from the original. regression_detects_original: true confirms the checker's own classification. What remains outside this limited contribution: the check's overall passed:false traces to documentation_directive_present: false with documentation_semantics_require_direct_review: true — the documentation directive is explicitly separate work and still missing — and the new_tests_on_original error is the regression's designed demonstration, not a test defect. No concrete defect in the saved test, its placement, its constructor call (allow_no_value=True), or its assertions is indicated by the evidence, so the contribution is ready to close; I am not submitting, since the overall check stays failed on the out-of-scope documentation requirement and that does not make this session's test work incomplete.
